declared_purpose: Create, read, edit and analyze Word/DOCX documents, including formatting, tables, images, conversions, comments and tracked changes. Explicit requirements include validation after creation, ordered unpack/edit/repack for editing, and author "Claude" unless the user requests another name (SKILL.md:2-22,61-78,294-334). Supporting metadata also declares text extraction, conversion and content analysis (_meta.json:4-9).

data_operations.operation: Read documents and persist extracted or converted derivatives
data_operations.data_scope: Document text, including tracked changes in the demonstrated pandoc command; converted DOCX, PDF and page images.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local pandoc, LibreOffice and Poppler processes; output.md, converted documents and page-image files.
data_operations.condition: Only the corresponding reading or conversion workflow. External programs' additional behavior is unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Create and persist a document with embedded images
data_operations.source: Generated document content and selected local image files
data_operations.data_scope: Document content, image bytes and supplied image alternative text.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local docx JavaScript component and generated DOCX file.
data_operations.condition: New-document creation; image reads occur when images are included. Validation after creation is explicitly required.

data_operations.operation: Extract and retain the complete Office archive
data_operations.source: Selected DOCX, PPTX or XLSX archive
data_operations.data_scope: All archive members, including content, metadata, comments, revision history, media and embedded files when present.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller-selected output directory; XML and relationship files are subsequently read and rewritten locally.
data_operations.condition: Unpack invocation. Extraction is required by the documented editing workflow; this function provides no cleanup of the unpacked directory.

data_operations.operation: Transform document XML and remove selected revision metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Text runs, tracked-change wrappers, author attributes, run revision identifiers and proofing markers. Same-author redlines may merge despite different timestamps.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Rewritten local word/document.xml; the original archive is unaffected.
data_operations.condition: DOCX unpacking enables both helpers by default; either can be disabled. Run merging removes run rsid attributes and proofErr elements. This is limited metadata removal, not document sanitization.

data_operations.source: Existing document XML and requested edits
data_operations.data_scope: Inserted text, retained deleted text, change identifiers, author names and dates.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Unpacked document XML and subsequently the packed DOCX.
data_operations.condition: Tracked-edit workflow. The default author requirement is explicit. A tracked deletion retains its text inside w:delText; it is not physical deletion.

data_operations.operation: Read comment structures and persist comments or replies
data_operations.source: Supplied comment text, author, initials, comment ID, optional parent ID and existing document parts
data_operations.data_scope: Comment text and attribution; generated UTC timestamp, random paragraph/durable IDs and reply relationships. Initials default to "C" rather than being inferred.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local word/comments.xml, commentsExtended.xml, commentsIds.xml, commentsExtensible.xml and related package declarations.
data_operations.condition: add_comment invocation. Parent lookup occurs after the comment is written, so a missing-parent error can leave the comment persisted.

data_operations.operation: Copy a document and request acceptance of tracked changes
data_operations.data_scope: Complete document and filesystem metadata copied by copy2; output path passed to LibreOffice.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requested output file and local LibreOffice process.
data_operations.condition: accept_changes invocation. The macro requests acceptance, storage and closure of the output document. The input remains. A timeout returns a success message without confirming the resulting document.

data_operations.operation: Create and reuse local runtime-support files
data_operations.source: Packaged LibreOffice macro and socket-shim source
data_operations.data_scope: Static support code; the shown writes do not contain document content.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/libreoffice_docx_profile/user/basic/Standard/Module1.xba and temporary-directory lo_socket_shim.c/lo_socket_shim.so; local LibreOffice and gcc processes.
data_operations.condition: Macro setup for acceptance; shim creation only when the AF_UNIX probe fails and no cached library exists. Successful compilation deletes the C source; the shared library and macro profile remain.

data_operations.operation: Read and pass the process environment to local subprocesses
data_operations.data_scope: All environment entries, with SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN set and conditional LD_PRELOAD replacement. Any credentials present would be included; none are enumerated by the source.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Returned environment dictionary and local LibreOffice subprocess. The conditional gcc invocation also uses normal inherited environment behavior.
data_operations.condition: get_soffice_env and run_soffice paths, including accept_changes. This is local process inheritance, not demonstrated remote disclosure.

data_operations.operation: Copy and repack all files into the output archive
data_operations.data_scope: Every file under that directory. XML condensation removes XML comment nodes and formatting whitespace; it does not remove Word review-comment parts or tracked deleted text.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary content copy and requested DOCX/PPTX/XLSX output archive.
data_operations.condition: Pack invocation. The temporary copy is context-managed for cleanup; the input directory and output remain. Validation runs only with an existing original file and validation enabled.

data_operations.operation: Read and validate document structures; optionally persist repairs
data_operations.source: Unpacked document parts or a selected packed Office file
data_operations.data_scope: XML, relationships, identifiers, content declarations and local file-existence information. Repairs rewrite whitespace attributes and invalid durable IDs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local validators and document directory. Packed-file validation extracts all members into a mkdtemp directory without supplied cleanup.
data_operations.condition: Validation CLI supports DOCX/PPTX and rejects XLSX after extraction. CLI repairs require --auto-repair; pack repairs run during enabled validation with an existing original. Pack's XLSX path constructs no validators. HTTP/mailto relationship targets are skipped by the shown file-reference check.

data_operations.source: Original Office archive supplied for comparison
data_operations.data_scope: Entire archive extracted for an individual original XML check, DOCX paragraph count or redlining comparison, although those operations subsequently use selected XML.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Separate context-managed local temporary directories; counts and comparison results reach the caller.
data_operations.condition: Original supplied. Per-file XSD failure invokes original extraction repeatedly. Redlining extraction occurs only if that validator is reached and its no-matching-author early exit does not apply; validator lists short-circuit on failure.

data_operations.operation: Infer the author of newly added tracked changes
data_operations.source: Author attributes and insertion/deletion counts in modified and original word/document.xml
data_operations.data_scope: Per-author counts, positive count differences and an inferred single author; ambiguous results include author/count mappings in an exception.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local helper caller and optionally RedliningValidator; pack prints an ambiguity warning to stderr.
data_operations.condition: Only direct helper use or explicit injection through infer_author_func. Packaged pack CLI does not supply this callback. This is an inferred document attribution, not verified personal identity.

data_operations.operation: Reconstruct document text and generate a local failure diff
data_operations.data_scope: Text reconstructed after reversing the selected author's changes in memory; complete reconstructed texts written to original.txt and modified.txt; paragraph-level diff output.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Context-managed local temporary text files, local git process and caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: Redlining comparison finds unequal text. In-memory removal/restoration does not delete or rewrite the source documents. A second git invocation is a conditional fallback when the first produces no usable content.

data_operations.source: Validation results, repair operations and LibreOffice errors
data_operations.data_scope: File paths, identifiers, text previews, validation errors, author attribution and captured LibreOffice stderr.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Function caller and local stdout/stderr; no separate remote logging destination is shown.
data_operations.condition: Corresponding errors, repairs or status reporting. Text previews and repair messages can appear without verbose mode. Caller-side retention is unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete extracted DOCX/PPTX, including metadata, comments, media and embedded files when present.
potential_excess.condition: Packed-file validation; no cleanup is supplied on success, failure or exit.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Validation requires temporary access, but the declared purpose does not require retaining an additional extracted document afterward.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep required parts available throughout validation and return useful results.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a context-managed temporary directory with cleanup around extraction and validation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep inputs and requested outputs intact; cleanup must also cover exceptions and validation failures. This narrows retention of a required action.

potential_excess.data_scope: Every member of a selected XLSX archive.
potential_excess.condition: A packed XLSX passes extension checks, is extracted, and then receives the unsupported-file-type error.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Rejecting an unsupported validation format requires its type, not its contents.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check supported validation types before creating a directory or opening the archive.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the rejection and supported DOCX/PPTX behavior. This removes a redundant data-processing action.

potential_excess.data_scope: Original archive members unrelated to the XML currently checked, including media, embeddings and other document parts.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Temporary directories used for original-file XSD checks, paragraph counting and redlining.
potential_excess.condition: Comparison validation extracts the whole original before reading one selected XML part.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These particular comparisons need the corresponding original XML, not every original archive member.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read the corresponding original XML and perform the same schema, paragraph or text comparison.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Read the needed ZIP member directly, or extract only the necessary members.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain missing-part handling and any demonstrated parsing dependencies. Keep whole-package checks where independently required. This narrows data within required comparisons.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated copies of the same complete original archive.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: A new temporary extraction for each XML file whose current XSD validation fails.
potential_excess.condition: Multiple current XML files fail validation and an original is available.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Baseline comparison requires each relevant original part; repeatedly extracting the entire unchanged archive is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Compute original baseline errors for every relevant part.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse one archive handle or scoped snapshot and cache baseline results during a validation run.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve every per-file comparison against the same original version. This removes repeated actions rather than dropping required checks.

potential_excess.data_scope: Environment entries unrelated to conversion, including credentials if present.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local LibreOffice subprocess environment; conditional local gcc subprocess environment.
potential_excess.condition: Parent environment contains entries unnecessary for these components.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The purpose requires document processing and runtime compatibility; the source establishes no need for unrelated credentials.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Supply executable discovery, required runtime/profile settings, SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN and conditional LD_PRELOAD.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Construct a tested environment allowlist or exclude unrelated credential variables before launching these subprocesses.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve required platform, locale, library and profile settings. This narrows a local process boundary; it is not evidence of remote credential transmission.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unchanged text within complete differing paragraphs.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Default redlining failure output printed to caller stdout.
potential_excess.condition: Reconstructed texts differ and git returns a diff. Text extraction puts each paragraph on one line, so zero line context still includes unchanged portions of that paragraph.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Failure diagnostics support correcting improperly tracked edits; all unchanged paragraph content need not be returned.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the mismatch and provide sufficient location and changed-text context to repair it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return bounded changed spans with short context; make the complete diff an explicit diagnostic option.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep validation failure and actionable diagnostics. This narrows data in a required diagnostic, not the comparison itself; the shown recipient is the caller.

potential_excess.data_scope: Attempted reply text, author, initials, timestamp and generated identifiers; potentially new comment declarations.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Unpacked comment XML and package declarations.
potential_excess.condition: Requested parent comment is absent; the helper writes the comment before returning the parent-not-found error.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Creating a reply requires a valid parent. Persisting a failed reply does not achieve that outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate the parent and persist a correctly linked reply only when valid.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Check parent existence before writes and commit related comment-part updates together.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve valid comments, replies and existing document parts. This removes an unnecessary failed-path write.

unknowns: The inventory contains no scripts/office/schemas files, although validators require them. Mapped XSD validation therefore lacks its required resources; schema correctness and optional metadata requirements remain unresolved (scripts/office/validators/base.py:43-59,97-97,748-783).

LibreOffice, pandoc, docx, Poppler, git, gcc and XML-library implementations are not supplied. Their implicit retrieval, telemetry, profile contents and additional retention are unknown. Static links and XML namespace identifiers alone do not establish remote disclosure.
No runtime documents or environment are supplied, so actual sensitive content and the presence of credential variables cannot be established.

Exact comment timestamps are automatically persisted, but their necessity for the requested document outcome and client compatibility is not established by the supplied source; missing schemas prevent resolving omission requirements.

Caller-side logging, onward disclosure, filesystem access controls, OS cleanup and secure erasure are unspecified. Ordinary stdout returns and local temporary files do not establish a remote recipient.
accept_changes reports success on subprocess timeout without checking the output. Whether all tracked changes were actually accepted on that path remains unresolved (scripts/accept_changes.py:76-87).
